Opportunities.title: What German temp work actually pays
Opportunities.subtitle: Five temporary-work profiles with their pay band, weekly hours, shifts and the level of German they ask for. Taken from 14 real job ads and from the sector's collective agreement — not from a promise.

meta.title: Real conditions of temporary work in Germany
meta.description: What warehouse, logistics, production, meat processing and agriculture pay per hour in Germany, what hours and shifts are worked, and what level of German is required. Based on 14 real job ads and the Zeitarbeit collective agreement.

disclosure.title: This is not a list of open vacancies
disclosure.body: There is no company behind these pages, no start date and no position to apply to. They describe the typical conditions of the German market for each profile: what it pays, what the work is and what is asked for. Real vacancies, once there are any, are published separately.
disclosure.source: Source: 14 job ads from Randstad, Adecco and Tempton reviewed on {date}, and the Zeitarbeit collective agreement (GVP/DGB). Sector pay rises on 1 September 2026 and again in April 2027, so these figures have a known expiry date.

agreement.title: The floor is set by the collective agreement, not by the agency
agreement.body: Temporary agency work in Germany has its own minimum wage, above the general one: {amount} gross per hour from {date}. An offer below that figure is not a bargain, it is illegal. It is the first thing worth checking, and it applies to all five profiles on this page.

ask.title: What almost no advert says, and you should ask
ask.intro: Of the 14 ads reviewed, none stated the exact weekly hours, none said whether accommodation was available and none said how long the contract lasts. These are the questions that decide whether moving is worth it:
items: How many hours a week? With hourly pay, the working week is half the wage: €16 an hour at 35 hours and at 40 hours are not the same month.
Is there accommodation, what does it cost, and is the amount written into the contract? A surprise payroll deduction is the sector's most repeated complaint.
What is the minimum contract length? "Temporary" with no term does not let you decide on a move.
Who signs the contract, the agency or the factory? In this sector a "permanent contract" almost always means permanent with the agency, which is not the same thing.
What level of German is required, measured? "Good German" is not a requirement, it is an opaque filter: only 3 of the 14 ads gave a CEFR level.

facts.basisObserved: Collective agreement floor and ceiling observed in the ads reviewed
facts.basisAgreement: Collective agreement floor. No observed range: we do not publish a ceiling we have not measured.

warehouse.title: Warehouse and forklift
warehouse.summary: The most common profile in the sample and the best paid without a qualification: a forklift licence is worth €0.50 to €1 more per hour.
warehouse.intro: Picking orders and moving goods in distribution centres in eastern Germany, almost always on three rotating shifts and 40 hours a week. Six of the fourteen ads reviewed are warehouse and logistics, and this is the block where the pay range is published most often. Three required a forklift licence (Staplerschein) and all three paid above the unqualified production band. The German asked for is shift German — signage, instructions, incidents — not office German.
tasks: Unload and put away goods with counterbalance and reach trucks
Pick orders using an RF handheld terminal
Check quantities and condition of incoming goods
Keep aisles and picking areas clear
Record movements in the warehouse system
requirements: EU citizenship
Forklift licence for the best-paid offers; an EU licence can be recognised, and one can also be obtained in Germany within a few days
German at A2, enough for signage and shift instructions
Availability for three rotating shifts, including nights
Previous experience welcome, rarely essential
conditions: Hourly and gross pay: it is the unit the whole sector publishes in, and nobody publishes monthly or net pay
Night, Sunday and public-holiday premiums on top of base pay, in 4 of the 14 ads
Up to 30 days' holiday a year, in 9 of the 14
Holiday and Christmas bonuses, in 8 of the 14
Free workwear and protective equipment, in 8 of the 14

logistics.title: Logistics and dispatch
logistics.summary: Loading, unloading and dispatch. It is the block that publishes its pay range most often of the three agencies reviewed.
logistics.intro: Moving goods between the dock, the warehouse and the lorry at sites in Thuringia and Saxony. In the sample these are three-shift, full-time roles, and this is where the pay range appears published most often: one of the three agencies reviewed always publishes it, another never does, and the third only when it is the hook. A forklift licence appears as a requirement in three of the six ads in this block.
tasks: Load and unload lorries with forklifts and pallet trucks
Check delivery notes and dispatch paperwork
Prepare, strap and wrap pallets for dispatch
Sort goods by route and destination
Report damage and discrepancies on receipt
requirements: EU citizenship
German at A2 for shift instructions and dispatch paperwork
Availability for three rotating shifts
Forklift licence, valued and sometimes required
Accuracy and the ability to work on your feet
conditions: Hourly and gross pay, with a minimum and a maximum in 5 of the 6 ads that give a figure
Premiums for night, Sunday and public-holiday work
Up to 30 days' holiday a year
The sector agreement (GVP/DGB) cited explicitly in 12 of the 14 ads
Workwear and protective equipment at the company's expense

production.title: Industrial production
production.summary: The most open profile: several ads state outright that no experience is needed and that training is given on site. Also the one that stretches furthest at the top.
production.intro: Line work in factories: feeding the machine, visual checks, packing and palletising. Eight of the fourteen ads reviewed are production roles, and this is where people without a trade get in. The range stretches a long way at the top when the client is a large industrial site on continuous shifts: the best paid in the sample, in Hamburg, reached €24.85 an hour, but required continuous shift work and a medical clearance, so it is not the figure to expect from a first job. It is also the block where a German requirement appears least often: three of the eight production ads gave no level at all.
tasks: Feed and monitor the production or packaging line
Visually check the product and remove defects
Weigh, label and palletise finished product
Clean the workstation at the end of the shift to protocol
Report line stoppages to the supervisor
requirements: EU citizenship
Manual dexterity and the ability to stand throughout the shift
Availability for morning and afternoon shifts, and for rotating shifts in the best-paid offers
Previous experience welcome; several ads state outright that it is not essential
The German requirement varies widely: from not stated at all to spoken and written
conditions: Hourly and gross pay; the floor in the sample matches the collective agreement floor, which is no coincidence
Continuous shifts and large industrial clients pay considerably more, and ask considerably more
Up to 30 days' holiday a year, plus holiday and Christmas bonuses
On-site training and protective equipment at the company's expense
A permanent contract with the agency in 6 of the 14 ads, and the option to join the client's payroll in 3

meat-processing.title: Meat processing
meat-processing.summary: One of the sectors that does recruit in Spain, and one of those not advertised on German portals — which is why it does not appear in the sample.
meat-processing.intro: Cutting, boning, packing and cleaning in meat plants. None of the fourteen ads reviewed is from this sector, and that is a finding in itself: it is not advertised through the domestic portals of the large German agencies, which does not mean there is no demand — it is in fact one of the sectors that does recruit in Spain. Since there is no observed range, we do not publish one here. What can be stated is the floor, because hiring is through a temporary work agency and the Zeitarbeit agreement applies.
tasks: Cutting and boning on the line
Sorting, weighing and grading cuts
Packing, labelling and palletising product
Cleaning and disinfecting the workstation to hygiene protocol
Visual quality control of the product
requirements: EU citizenship
Ability to work standing in a cold environment
Food hygiene training, normally provided on arrival
Availability for morning and afternoon shifts
The sample reviewed does not document the German level for this sector
conditions: Zeitarbeit agreement floor: {floor} gross per hour from {floorDate}
No observed range: we do not publish a ceiling we have not measured
Weekly hours, accommodation, transport and contract length are set by each agency, and are worth asking for in writing before accepting

agriculture.title: Agriculture and packing
agriculture.summary: Seasonal work, and the profile where it matters most who signs the contract: that determines which minimum wage applies.
agriculture.intro: Harvesting, greenhouse work, grading and packing on farms. It does not appear in the sample either, for the same reason as meat processing. There is a warning here that matters more than on any other profile: the Zeitarbeit floor applies when a temporary work agency hires you, which is how this site works; seasonal work hired directly by the farm falls under the general minimum wage, which in 2026 is lower. If an advert does not say who signs the contract, that is the first question to ask.
tasks: Harvesting and handling in the field or greenhouse
Grading product by size and quality
Packing, labelling and preparing orders for dispatch
Keeping the facilities clean and tidy
Recording quantities and waste
requirements: EU citizenship
Ability to do physical work outdoors and on your feet
Seasonal availability, with peaks during the campaign
Previous experience welcome, not essential
The sample reviewed does not document the German level for this sector
conditions: Zeitarbeit agreement floor: {floor} gross per hour from {floorDate}, provided the employer is a temporary work agency
No observed range: we do not publish a ceiling we have not measured
Hired directly by the farm, the lower general minimum wage applies: always ask who signs
